title: About shows 6.1.0 but drops the build number, and System Information omits everything a support ticket needs
what_happened: About reports 'Version 6.1.0'. The shipped desktop version is 6.1.0+25 (apps/desktop/pubspec.yaml:4) -- the build number, the one field that distinguishes two builds of the same release, is not shown. 'System Information' lists only Platform / OS Version / Dart Version. It does not list the Rust bridge version, the database schema version, the data directory, the active backend, or the release channel, all of which are the first things asked for on a bug report.
expected: NINA's About shows version+build+commit and a one-click 'copy system info'. Show '6.1.0 (build 25)', add schema version / data dir / bridge version, and give the card a Copy button.
proposed_fix: Render '${appVersion.version} (build ${appVersion.buildNumber})' and extend the System Information card; add a copy-to-clipboard action.

title: Seven paired devices are all called 'Android companion' with no way to tell them apart before revoking
what_happened: The Paired Devices list shows 7 identical rows: title 'Android companion', subtitle 'Android phone or tablet', 'Not seen yet', 'No connection recorded yet', differing only by a paired-on date. There is no IP, no last-seen, no device model, no scope, and no rename. Revoking the phone you sold is guesswork.
expected: Show last-seen, last IP, granted scope (the DB already stores auth_grant_spec -- one of these devices holds 'admin' and the UI never says so) and allow renaming. NINA/ASIAIR-class tools name the client and show when it last talked.
proposed_fix: Render auth_grant_spec as a badge, add last-seen/IP, and add a rename action.

title: Import failures are reported as raw Dart exception text ('Import failed: FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 1)')
what_happened: Equipment Profiles > import (the download-arrow button next to New Profile) accepts any file. Choosing a non-JSON file shows the snackbar 'Import failed: FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 1)'; choosing a syntactically valid but unrelated JSON shows 'Import failed: FormatException: Profile name must be a non-empty string'. Both are the raw toString() of the thrown exception.
expected: 'That file is not a Skotiq profile export' plus the file name. The exported JSON also carries no format marker or version field at all (I exported one and read it: it is a bare map of profile fields), so the importer has nothing to check against and cannot warn about profiles exported by a newer build.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > import icon > pick any .txt. Then pick a JSON that is not a profile.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/equipment_profiles_screen_parts/profile_controls.dart (import handler) and the profile toJson used by Export
proposed_fix: Add {"format":"skotiq.equipment-profile","version":1} to the export and validate it on import; map failures to plain-language messages.

title: 'Restore' asks you to restart the app afterwards but does not offer to, and nothing on the screen stays to remind you
what_happened: The restore result is a transient snackbar: 'Restored 123 items. Restart Skotiq before the next run.' Once it fades there is no indication anywhere that the running app is now showing stale in-memory state that disagrees with the database -- and the whole point of restoring is usually that you are about to observe. There is no Restart button.
expected: Either reload the providers after a restore (the app already rebuilds them on profile switch) or show a persistent banner with a 'Restart now' action.
repro: Settings > Backup & Restore > restore icon on any bundle > Restore. Wait 5 seconds; the message is gone and the screen looks normal.
proposed_fix: Persistent banner + 'Restart now', or invalidate the affected providers in place.

title: A 426 MB abandoned GLADE download sat in the catalog directory for six weeks with nothing in the UI acknowledging it
what_happened: ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/catalogs contained glade_plus_galaxies.csv.partial at 426,030,763 bytes dated Jun 17, alongside a 0-byte glade_plus_galaxies.csv. The Catalogs page showed GLADE+ as not installed and offered a fresh download, with no mention that 407 MiB of a previous attempt was still on disk and no way to reclaim it from the UI. (It is deleted when a new download starts -- I watched it vanish the moment I pressed Download -- so the space is recovered only by attempting another download, which currently cannot succeed.)
expected: Show 'Partial download: 407 MB - Resume / Discard' on the card, or clean up partials on launch. Deep-sky users on small SSDs care about half a gigabyte.
where: the annotation catalog download service's partial-file handling
proposed_fix: Surface and offer to resume or delete partials; sweep stale .partial files at startup.

title: The Deep-Star Tier card tells an astrophotographer to build and host their own tileset with a repo tool
what_happened: Settings > Catalogs > 'Deep-Star Tier (Tycho-2 / Gaia)' reads: 'Streams faint stars below the bundled HYG floor (~mag 11.5) as view-culled tiles when zoomed in. Host a tileset built with tools/catalog_prep and point the URL below at it.' That is an instruction to a developer with a checkout of this repository, shipped verbatim in a consumer settings page. There is no default host, no 'get one from Skotiq' option, and no explanation of what happens if you do not.
expected: Ship or host a tileset and make this one toggle. If self-hosting really is the only path, say so honestly ('No public tileset is available yet; advanced users can host their own') and link documentation rather than a source path.
repro: Settings > Catalogs > scroll to Deep-Star Tier.
proposed_fix: Provide a default tileset URL or reword for a non-developer audience.

title: Replay & Debug is written for the developer who built it: a lowercase title sentence and two user-facing dialogs that name a database table
what_happened: The page header reads 'Replay Debug' with the subtitle 'decision-log retention + cleanup for the retrospective Replay screen.' -- lowercase first word, a '+' used as a conjunction. The logging toggle's help text says decisions are 'persisted to the sequence_decisions table', and the destructive confirmation says 'This deletes every row in the sequence_decisions table.' The confirm dialog also does not say how many rows it is about to delete (there were 3), and its 'Clear' action is rendered as plain blue text identical to 'Cancel', whereas the equivalent profile-delete dialog uses a filled red 'Delete' button.
expected: Sentence-cased prose that never names a SQL table; 'This will delete 3 recorded decisions' in the confirmation; and one consistent destructive-button style across dialogs.
repro: Settings > search 'replay' > Replay & Debug. Read the header. Press 'Clear all replay history'.
proposed_fix: Rewrite the copy for users, add the row count to the confirmation, and use the shared destructive-button variant.

title: Enter does not submit the profile dialogs, so the fastest path through them is mouse-only
what_happened: In the Duplicate Profile dialog the name field is focused and pre-filled; pressing Enter does nothing -- the dialog stays open and no profile is created (DB unchanged). You must move to the mouse and click Duplicate.
expected: Enter submits, Escape cancels. That is the convention in every dialog of this shape, and these dialogs are one-field.
repro: Settings > Equipment Profiles > overflow > Duplicate > press Return. Nothing happens; the dialog is still up.
proposed_fix: Give the TextField an onSubmitted that fires the primary action.
